thread:
maya: heads-up, nightly CI shows a tokens/s drop for paged-attn at 8k. looks like a DRAM surge.
dinesh: numbers?
maya: paste from benchbot + perf counters:
``
bench: paged-attn bs=4 seq=8192
kernel=flashv2_paged tokens/s=47.8k (-21%) DRAM_bw=470GB/s L2_bw=2.0GB/s sm_eff=0.60
kernel=flashfuse tokens/s=60.5k (ref) DRAM_bw=385GB/s sm_eff=0.72
kv_hitrate=0.69 (was ~0.91)
eviction_spike@step=3
``

rachel: kv hitrate drop would definitely push more DRAM traffic. evictions + paged loads ~= extra roundtrips.

frank: also check shared mem per-block; if smem is high we reduce occupancy and increase DRAM pressure via spills.

maya: current flashv2_paged smem ~50KB/block -> occupancy ~0.48 on Turing gen. that matches sm_eff.

frank: try retiling to 64x16 or 32x32 to lower per-block shared mem and see occupancy change. also test `--max-registers=64` to drop reg pressure.

dinesh: I'll run microprofile (nvprof-like) and capture bank-conflict heatmap + `dram__throughput` traces.

maya: queued a bench with tile=64x16 + kv_prefetch=1 + microbatch(split=2 for seq>4096). job: benchbot-8793.

benchbot: [queued] benchbot-8793 started on pool-c

ops-bot: recommend creating a canary fallback route for paged-attn (flashfuse) at 10% while triaging.

maya: agreed. creating playbook + canary route now.

maya: first 20m results: tokens/s 47.8k -> 55.9k with tile change + prefetch, DRAM_bw down to 415GB/s, sm_eff 0.69, kv_hitrate 0.81.

rachel: progress. still shy of flashfuse baseline. next try frank's reg patch + bank stride mitigation.

frank: note: bank stride mitigation (`smem_bank_stride=2`) reduced conflict cost on earlier Pascal runs. worth trying.

dinesh: once I have nvprof output I'll upload the heatmaps to /infra/bench/repro/paged-dram-spike/ and link here.

maya: ops-bot created canary `attn.paged.canary` -> 10% -> kernel=flashfuse ttl=2h. tagging infra and oncall.

ops-bot: alert rule suggestion: `dram__throughput > 420GB/s` for paged-attn routes -> auto page eng-runtime.

maya: dropping full perf artifacts in ~45m. ping me for early access. :thumbsup:
